summary.text: Son of Eetion (`eetion-cilicia`), a rich man and a valiant whom Hector honoured above all the people as his comrade and welcome companion at the feast — slain by Menelaus as he stood over Patroclus' body in the fight for the corpse.

story.text: When Hector stood over Patroclus and hurled his bright spear, Athena filled his dark heart with daring. Among the Trojans was Podes, son of Eetion, a rich man and a valiant, and Hector honoured him above all the people, for that he was his comrade, a welcome companion at the feast. Fair-haired Menelaus smote him upon the belt with a spear cast as he started to flee, and drave the bronze clean through and out at the navel; he fell with a thud and his armour clanged upon him.
